title: Blueprint `sk-thm-sp-qbar`: **smooth purity** (SGA 4, Exposé XVIII, Théorème 3.2.5): the adjoint of the trace, `ℚ̄_ℓ,X(d)[2d] ⟶ Rf^! ℚ̄_ℓ,Y`, is an is
statement:
Let $\ell$ be a prime and $k$ a field of characteristic $p>0$ with $p\ne\ell$. Let $X,Y$ be separated finite-type $k$-schemes and let $f:X\to Y$ be a $k$-morphism smooth of pure relative dimension $d\in\mathbf N$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-setting, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Put $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ and $B_T=p_T^*\underline\Omega$, where $\underline\Omega$ is the finite-extension-valued condensed coefficient ring [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Write $\mathcal C_T\subset D(\operatorname{Mod}_{B_T})$ for its full bounded constructible category, $F=Rf_!:\mathcal C_X\to\mathcal C_Y$ for the chosen compactification functor [sk-def-sfb-dc-lower-shriek], and $G=Rf^!$ for its chosen right adjoint, with unit $\eta$ and counit $\varepsilon$ [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek]. Let $T_d\in\mathcal C_X$ be the shifted Tate object whose underlying complex is $\mathrm{tateTwistDerived}(X,\ell,d)[2d]$ [def-pur-condensed-tate-twists]; it lies in $\mathcal C_X$ because $\ell$ is invertible on $X$ [lem-route-bounded-constructible-tate-twist-derived-of-invertible].

Use the normalized smooth trace constructed as follows, fixing its meaning rather than choosing an arbitrary morphism. For $n\geq1$ put $L_n=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_Y$ and $M_n=(\mathbf Z/\ell^n\mathbf Z)_X(d)[2d]$, with their quotient and root-power transitions and the diagonal/deformation purity maps $\phi_n:M_n\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_n^!L_n$ [lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base]. Let $L=R\varprojlim L_n$, $M=R\varprojlim M_n$ be the normalized integral objects [lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower], and $U_T$ the integral-to-condensed realization of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction]. Use its specified counit-preserving comparison $c_0:U_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}G(U_YL)$. Let $u:U_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_Y$ and $a:U_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}T_d$ be the canonical unit and Tate comparisons of [lem-pur-condensed-tate-realization], read in the full constructible categories. Put $c=G(u)\circ c_0$ and define
$$t_f=\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_Y}\circ F(c)\circ F(a^{-1}):F(T_d)\longrightarrow\mathbf1_Y.$$
This is the normalized smooth trace denoted $\mathrm{smoothTrace}\,\ell\,f\,d$ in the upstream construction. Its adjoint
$$\alpha_f=\operatorname{Hom}_{F\dashv G}(t_f):T_d\longrightarrow G\mathbf1_Y,$$
namely $\mathrm{smoothPurityMap}\,\ell\,f\,d$, is an isomorphism in $\mathcal C_X$.

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-finite-smooth-adjunction-general-base] to this $k,f,d$. It gives the actual diagonal/deformation isomorphisms $\phi_n$ and the exceptional coefficient comparisons, including their quotient cocycle. By [lem-pur-condensed-tate-integral-tower] their sources and the units form normalized towers with compatible etale-origin witnesses, constructible cohomology and common bounds; their derived limits $M,L$ are completed integral constructible with the required canonical reductions. In particular every $M_n$ is concentrated in the single degree $r=-2d$. The native Over(Spec k) instantiation is now proved by the private helper smoothTrace_reconstructionInputs: it installs the two scheme-over structures, transports the six finiteness instances from X.hom and Y.hom, uses Over.w f for the morphism-over instance, derives positive characteristic from primality, and applies condensedTateIntegralTower. Its result retains the finite diagonal/deformation system and normalized Tate/unit reconstructions. No witness is extracted into a definition. Further native finite glue is proved by smoothTrace_finiteQuotientSquare: the supplied ReductionData.pro_purity square is composed with the coefficient-unit reduction, pro_natural moves that unit reduction across the lower-level gamma, and lem-pur-finite-source-unit-reduction identifies the remaining source arrow with the actual root tensor quotient. This proves the specified finite gamma quotient square, including equal levels, without asserting that the unconstructed smoothTrace already realizes it. The new smoothTrace_normalizedFiniteSystem then extracts the positive Level family and its ReductionData from that same native reconstruction result, reindexes the levels by n+1, proves all of these quotient squares by the preceding helper, and retains ReconstructionResult for the identical compactification and finiteness witnesses. Thus the actual supplied finite system, its unit quotient squares, and the theorem reconstructing these inputs are simultaneously available in Lean, with witnesses extracted only inside a proof. The native finite inverse square is now proved by smoothTrace_gammaUnit_isIso and smoothTrace_finiteInverseQuotientSquare: finite purity at the constructible unit makes gammaUnit invertible; cancel the scalar image of the upper gamma, apply the already proved forward quotient square, and cancel the lower gamma. This retains the actual root quotient map, including equal levels. The private theorem smoothTrace_normalizedIntegralSystem now instantiates that retained ReconstructionResult with exactly the extracted finite levels and quotient comparisons. It simultaneously retains the strict Tate and unit towers, their specified level identifications, the two ProjectionNormalized assertions, the two Reconstructed assertions, and IdentifiesExceptional. For the same witnesses it proves every inverse exceptional quotient square, including equal levels. The extraction occurs wholly in a proof, and neither the trace choice nor the disputed purity instance is used.

source.place: Steps 1–2: finite diagonal/deformation purity and normalized integral towers

proof.text: Apply case (b) of [lem-pur-condensed-exceptional-reconstruction] with $L,M_\bullet,\phi_n$ from Step 1 and $r=-2d$. All normalization, intertwining, constructibility, common-bound and completed-integral hypotheses were supplied there. This yields the specified isomorphism $c_0:U_XM\to G(U_YL)$ for the actual bounded constructible condensed right adjoint. Its counit is induced by the finite counits, so this is the normalized comparison used in the trace, with no arbitrary choice of a purity witness. The native representability-to-isomorphism step is now proved by smoothTrace_representingTranspose_isIso, before the disputed instance: naturality identifies postcomposition by the actual adjunct with the specified representing Hom bijection followed by the actual adjunction bijection. The Yoneda criterion then proves invertibility, without assuming any comparison isomorphism. The inverse compatibility of the actual reconstructed gamma maps is now proved by smoothTrace_reconstructedInverseQuotientSquare. Its hypothesis is the previously supplied IdentifiesExceptional for the actual derived limit. The conclusion says that the scalar image of the higher inverse gamma followed by the canonical reduction normalization equals the actual finite exceptional reduction followed by the lower inverse gamma. Cancel the invertible scalar image of the higher gamma, use the forward reconstructed square, and cancel the lower inverse. Thus both directions of the reduction-system comparison have actual Lean proofs. Transport from this integral coefficient presentation to the exceptional reconstruction Context and construction of the chosen smoothTrace still remain. The private theorem smoothTrace_reconstructedInverseSemilinearSquare also transposes the inverse quotient square under the actual coefficient extension/restriction adjunction. Naturality in source and target gives the semilinear compatibility needed for inverse maps of the exceptional reduction systems; no arbitrary derived-system lift is asserted. The private smoothTrace_exceptionalSingleDegree now converts the retained IdentifiesExceptional cohomology vanishing into both standard t-structure bounds at degree -2d for every actual finite exceptional unit. The private smoothTrace_exceptionalHomology_bijective applies the existing proved truncation Hom bijection to any source bounded above at -2d and that exceptional target. Thus H^(-2d) both determines a derived map and lifts a specified cohomology map uniquely. The private smoothTrace_nativeExceptionalHomology extracts the actual finite levels and compactification from the unchanged smoothTrace_normalizedFiniteSystem theorem and instantiates its retained ReconstructionResult to obtain the reconstructed Tate object and supplies these bijections together with their retained IdentifiesExceptional proof. The original normalized-system theorem still supplies all strict tower, projection, reconstruction and inverse quotient data unchanged. This is the finite single-degree Hom step of case (b); no claim that an arbitrary family of derived maps lifts to a whole derived-system map is made. The strict-system transport and actual trace normalization remain to be supplied.

source.place: Steps 2–3: reconstruct the counit-preserving condensed exceptional comparison

proof.text: Apply [lem-pur-condensed-tate-realization] to $M$ on $X$ and to $L$ on $Y$ with $d=0$. Its completed-integral and canonical-reduction hypotheses hold by Step 1. This gives $a:U_XM\xrightarrow{\sim}T_d$ and $u:U_YL\xrightarrow{\sim}\mathbf1_Y$. These ambient comparisons lift to the full constructible categories: lift each arrow and its inverse by fullness; faithfulness then lifts both inverse equations. The full-subcategory assertion is part of [prop-weil-pbc-qbar-condensed-two-colimit]. Thus $c=G(u)\circ c_0$ is an isomorphism, with inverse $c_0^{-1}\circ G(u^{-1})$. The full-faithfulness and inverse-composition glue is now proved in smoothPurityMap_of_reconstructed_trace. Given the actual realized object M, its ambient Tate realization a, the constructible comparison c (including the target-unit factor), and the specified trace formula, lift a with the existing fully faithful inclusion, construct e = lift(a)^(-1) followed by c, identify the actual adjunct with e.hom, and prove that its ambient inverse is mapIso(c.symm) followed by a. The geometric construction of c and the trace formula are still required inputs. The helper smoothTrace_from_representing_pairing now constructs this comparison from an explicit representing pairing t:F(M)->L, its Hom bijections, the ambient Tate identification a and target-unit identification u. It lifts a by full faithfulness, obtains c0 as the actual transpose of t, proves c0 invertible by the preceding Yoneda argument, and forms e=lift(a)^(-1);c0;G(u). The inverse adjunction law and naturality prove F(e);epsilon=F(lift(a)^(-1));t;u. This is actual Lean construction, with no comparison selected from a bare existence theorem. The geometric pairing, Tate and target-unit identifications remain inputs. The private smoothTrace_normalizedComparison_unique now strengthens the formal assembly to uniqueness for the supplied representing pairing and its specified source and target isomorphisms. It constructs e from the actual transpose and proves uniqueness by injectivity of the inverse adjunction Hom equivalence. smoothTrace_from_representing_pairing now uses that result, retaining precisely its original statement and trace formula. This does not choose a geometric pairing from a mere existence assertion. The existing smoothPurityMap_of_reconstructed_trace proof now names its lifted isomorphism and composite and proves its two equations separately, preserving exactly the prior result; this avoids expensive elaboration of the nested constructor.

source.place: Step 2: identify the reconstructed Tate object and coefficient unit

proof.text:
Set $h=c\circ a^{-1}:T_d\to G\mathbf1_Y$. The defining trace is $t_f=\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_Y}\circ F(h)$. For the adjunction of [sk-def-sfb-dc-upper-shriek], its transpose is $G(t_f)\circ\eta_{T_d}$. Naturality of $\eta$ and the triangle identity give
$$G(t_f)\circ\eta_{T_d}=G(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_Y})\circ GF(h)\circ\eta_{T_d}=G(\varepsilon_{\mathbf1_Y})\circ\eta_{G\mathbf1_Y}\circ h=h.$$
Hence $\alpha_f=c\circ a^{-1}$ for this specific trace, not just for some trace with isomorphic source. The formal passage from this explicit counit formula to invertibility is proved in the source module by the private helper isIso_smoothPurityMap_of_trace_formula: it applies homEquiv to the inverse hom-equivalence formula, obtains alpha_f=h, and transports IsIso along that equality. The helper takes the comparison isomorphism and trace equality explicitly; it neither constructs nor chooses them. The geometric comparisons and normalized trace formula in the preceding steps remain to be supplied. The existing Lean attachment also still omits the intended smoothness binder, as recorded by the statement dispute in the source module and the B4 report. The general identity without invertibility is proved by smoothPurityMap_eq_of_trace_formula; isIso_smoothPurityMap_of_trace_formula now consumes this proved identity. The reconstructed isomorphism helper constructs its e before the disputed instance is declared, so this part does not use that instance. The private helper isIso_smoothPurityMap_of_representing_pairing now combines that constructed e and its counit formula with an explicit equation identifying the chosen smoothTrace with the realized pairing. It proves invertibility of the actual smoothPurityMap without assuming a geometric comparison isomorphism. The actual trace definition and this geometric identification still require construction; no original hole is claimed closed. A further obstruction is certified in the native category by smoothTrace_representing_not_unique_at_point. For the identity map of a separably closed point, the canonical open-unit comparison supplies a representing trace. Precomposition by minus the identity supplies another, and both induce all Hom bijections. Evaluation of the regular condensed module at a singleton shows minus one differs from one; faithful point pullback, the faithful single functor and the unit comparisons transport this distinction to the actual bounded constructible unit. Thus the unnormalized predicate in existsUnique_smoothTrace is false even in dimension zero. The current choice in smoothTrace is not a construction of the specified finite-normalized trace. This counterexample uses neither existsUnique_smoothTrace nor the disputed purity instance. No hole is closed by appealing to their inconsistency.

source.place: Step 3: counit-compatible identification with the chosen exceptional adjoint

proof.text: The inverse of $\alpha_f=c\circ a^{-1}$ is $\beta_f=a\circ c^{-1}$. Indeed $\beta_f\circ\alpha_f=a\circ c^{-1}\circ c\circ a^{-1}=1_{T_d}$ and $\alpha_f\circ\beta_f=c\circ a^{-1}\circ a\circ c^{-1}=1_{G\mathbf1_Y}$. These equations hold in $\mathcal C_X$ itself, proving the requested $\operatorname{IsIso}(\mathrm{smoothPurityMap}\,\ell\,f\,d)$. The inverse formula for the actual defined smoothPurityIso, conditional on the explicitly supplied reconstructed trace formula, is proved by smoothPurityIso_eq_of_reconstructed_trace. No original sorry is closed by this partial formalization.

All existing public signatures, attributes, data bodies and public imports are preserved. Two original holes remain and none is added. The unconditional purity signature and unnormalized representing-trace choice remain disputed; no contradiction is used to prove a hole. The added TStructure import is private and supplies only the proved categorical Hom theorem.
